name: Zechariah
overview: Zechariah was a male Levite belonging to the Izharite clan, a branch descending from Kohath, son of Levi. He is uniquely identified as the son of Isshiah, situating him within the priestly divisions established in Israel. His lineage connects him to the sacred duties entrusted to the Levites in the service of the tabernacle and later the temple.
namesAndTitles: The name Zechariah means 'YHWH remembers,' reflecting a theologically rich designation that emphasizes God's faithfulness and remembrance. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:25 and was not given directly by God but carries significant spiritual meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Zechariah as the son of Isshiah, establishing a clear paternal relationship. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text concerning Zechariah.
scriptureSignificance: Zechariah's significance lies in his role within the Levitical priesthood, specifically as an Izharite, which highlights his part in the structured priestly divisions. His identification as the son of Isshiah in 1 Chronicles 24:25 situates him within the organized system God ordained for temple service, underscoring the continuity of God's covenantal worship through faithful priestly families.
